extracted.intended_audience: Prospective Berkeley Math Circle students and their families (elementary through high school) and applicants to MTRW/BMC programs
extracted.subtask_description: Program information, application rules, expectations, schedules, fees, and policies for the Berkeley Math Circle (particularly the MTRW program) aimed at applicants and their families. Covers selection criteria, assessment structure, attendance/commitment rules, and operational contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program mission / aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Emulating famous Eastern European models, the program aims at drawing kids to mathematics, preparing them for mathematical contests, introducing them to the wonders of beautiful mathematical theories, and encouraging them to undertake future careers linked with mathematics, whether as mathematicians, mathematics educators, economists, or business entrepreneurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the overarching goals that guide content and selection: attract students to mathematics, prepare for contests, expose to beautiful theory, and encourage math-related careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTRW curriculum and learning goals
rubrics_metrics.description: MATH TAUGHT THE RIGHT WAY is intellectually demanding, interweaves algebra and geometry with general problem-solving and writing skills, does NOT conform to generic U.S. labels of math classes, and by the end of 9th grade surpasses the regular U.S. math curriculum in breadth, depth, and rigor. Learning to 'read and write mathematics' is emphasized as the basis for communicating mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation of content: integrated algebra/geometry/problem-solving/proofs, higher-than-standard rigor by grade 9, and emphasis on mathematical communication (writing). This functions as a quality standard for instructors and student outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Most instructors at the MTRW have PhD, MA, or BA degrees in math or other related degrees in science and are distinguished teachers at the Berkeley Math Circle, universities, and renowned middle and high schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectation that instruction is delivered by experienced, highly-qualified educators (advanced degrees and distinguished teaching backgrounds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment structure (homework, finals, report cards)
rubrics_metrics.description: MTRW students submit homework to be graded each week in each of three subjects: algebra, geometry, and proofs/problem solving. There are final exams in each subject. Report cards include the percentage of successfully completed regular and bonus work, as well as statistics for the corresponding classes, a list of top performers, and some special awards from instructors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies frequency and subjects of assessment, what finals exist, and the contents of report cards (percentages, class statistics, top performers, awards). Implicitly signals student workload and evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection / admissions criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection process is based on high academic qualifications and a timely and complete application, including payment sent through PayPal upon acceptance. Readmission for current students is not guaranteed. We will select only those who have shown dedication and growth in the program. We also expect to accept some very strong new students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions depend on demonstrated academic strength, timely/completed application (including payment upon acceptance), prior dedication/growth for returning students, and limited openings; being a current student does not ensure re-admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application phases, deadlines, and invoice due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase 1: Now through Tuesday, April 21st — Application decisions will be sent on Friday, April 24th — Invoice Due by Monday, April 27th at 12pm. Phase 2: Wednesday, April 22nd thru Tuesday, April 28th — Application decisions (pending space) will be sent on Friday, May 1st — Invoice Due by Monday, May 4th at 12pm. Phase 3: Wednesday, April 29th and thereafter — Application decisions (pending space) will be sent as space in the groups and classrooms allow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement: applicants must follow phase-specific windows and pay invoices by stated due dates to secure placement; decisions are communicated on specified dates or 'pending space' thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program schedule and meeting logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: MTRW Fall 2026 program will start on August 24th and meet on Mondays until December 14th. In total, there are 15 class meetings, all on Mondays from 5-8pm. Final Exams will be conducted during the last two weeks of classes, at a schedule and in modes (in person or take-home), as determined by the instructors. Families cannot request make-up Finals or alternative final exams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies program length, meeting days/times, final exam window and modes, and the strict no-makeup/alternative finals policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance and commitment expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that the space in the MTRW is very limited to the classrooms that we receive and all slots fill up quite quickly. If you are not sure you would like to participate in MTRW, you should NOT apply. If you are applying to MTRW just to 'try it out,' you should not apply. Spaces should be given to the most dedicated families who are ready to commit to rigorous mathematical education and have no doubts about their commitment, schedule, or situation in Fall 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to commit fully for the term; casual or tentative applicants are discouraged because capacity is limited and priority is given to dedicated families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional mode policy and contingency planning
rubrics_metrics.description: We anticipate that MTRW sessions in the Fall 2026 semester will be held IN-PERSON, possibly with occasional online sessions as needed. Depending on local and/or national guidelines, we may re-introduce masking or even online classes if needed. Families must commit to attending in-person AND any online sessions of MTRW in Fall 2026, regardless of when/whether a change of mode may occur. It is possible, but unlikely, that a move to remote classes would be necessary for some MTRW groups but not for others, in which case siblings may be split between attending on campus and attending online at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational policy: expect in-person learning with possible temporary shifts; families must accept mode changes and possible sibling splits across modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and refund policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are the fees for the MTRW Fall 2026 Program: $910 for the 6A, 7A, 8A, or 9A full programs; $303 for the 9A Proofs only program. Once enrolled and students have paid their enrollment fees, no refunds will be provided to families, regardless of changed personal circumstances or if sessions move between in-person and online modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial requirement: specified tuition rates and strict no-refund policy after payment, even if instructional mode changes or personal circumstances change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication / contact policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Please, DO NOT contact MTRW staff with non-emergency questions at any time. Ignoring this policy may hurt your admission chances. We do NOT reply to email inquiries as we do NOT have the resources to answer questions from hundreds of families via email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should avoid non-emergency contact; excessive inquiries are discouraged and may negatively influence admissions; the program does not provide email support for routine questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: BMC-Upper program closure notice and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Thank you for your interest in the BMC-Upper program. Unfortunately, due to UC Berkeley requirements and circumstances outside of our control, BMC-Upper is closing and will not be offered beginning in Fall 2025. BMC-Upper relies on the diverse array of guest speakers that give both in-person and virtual talks to our students, so the stringent fingerprinting requirements imposed upon us by the university severely limited our ability to put on our Spring 2024 program with a reduced speaker pool and would require us to change the program fundamentally to survive long term. That being said, we do hope to restart BMC-Upper in the future and remain in negotiations for a sustainable agreement that will allow us to continue to nurture a love of mathematics in students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational status and policy note explaining program suspension due to external requirements (fingerprinting), effect on guest speaker availability, and indication of possible future restart pending negotiations.
